newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast power rises on higher oil, natgas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast power rises on higher oil, natgas.

text.p: Wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Northeast rose Tuesday amid a rally in natural gas prices and unseasonal strength in residual fuel oil values, market source said.
Despite relatively flat usage of natgas and fuel oil by the region's utilities, higher costs to replace those fuels for generation firmed spot values, they said.
Today's surge in natgas prices was triggered by fears over a tropical depression in the Caribbean could threaten U.S. Gulf natgas supplies.
NYMEX November Henry Hub natgas futures closed at $2.470, up 17.0 cents per million British thermal units.
The domestic resid market remained buoyant by Monday's jump in crude prices amid renewed violence in Iraq's northern Kurdish areas.
"It's oil that's having the impact," said a Northeast trader, noting the marginal cost of power production in the Northeast in November is based more on resid than natgas prices.

Maine Yankee nuclear power plant resumption to 90 percent of its 910 megawatt output over the weekend had little effect on prices today. The generating station in Wiscasset, Maine, was tripped off line last Wednesday during routine testing of its reactor protective system.
"I think it affected only a few players," said another Northeast trader, referring to the three-day outage.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday delivered to Northeast Utilities' territory border was assessed at $33.00-$33.50 a megawatt hour, up from Monday's $31.00-$32.00 range.
Off-peak, non-firm NEPOOL power for Wednesday was pegged at $20.00-$22.00, wider than Monday's quote of $21.00-$22.00.
In the New York Power Pool (NYPP), peak, non-firm delivered in the western part of the system for Wednesday was valued at $19.00-$20.00, flat from Monday's levels.
Off-peak, non-firm electricity for delivery into western NYPP was talkedd near $14.00, also unchanged from Monday.
Prices in the western NYPP were flat because the generation capacity in that part of the state is either hydro or nuclear.
In eastern NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday was discussed at $29.00-$30.00, sharply higher than Monday's $26.00-$27.00.
Off-peak, non-firm NYPP power into eastern NYPP for next-day delivery was quoted near $17.00, compared with Monday's quote of $15.50-$16.60.
